header: Why Arabic dubbing is better in Modern Standard Arabic?
summary: Why Arabic dubbing is better in Modern Standard Arabic? Every Arab country has its own distinct Arabic accent, nevertheless all Arab countries share one mutual accent that is Modern Standard Arabic (also known as MSA). But when it comes to…
content:
Why Arabic dubbing is better in Modern Standard Arabic?

Every Arab country has its own distinct Arabic accent, nevertheless all Arab countries share one mutual accent that is Modern Standard Arabic (also known as MSA). But when it comes to MSA pronunciation, Lebanese voiceover talents are the best speakers in MSA, because unlike every other Arabic accent, the Lebanese accent has all letters in common with MSA. That’s why Belfay Studios, with its all Lebanese actors crew, and 25 years of experience in Arabic Dubbing can get the job done in the most proper way possible. With all respect for other Arabic recording studios.

Modern Standard Arabic for a wider and more widespread market in Arabic dubbing.

لماذا الدبلجة العربية أفضل في اللغة العربية الفصحى الحديثة؟

لكل دولة عربية لهجتها العربية المتميزة الخاصة بها، ومع ذلك تشترك جميع الدول العربية في لهجة متبادلة واحدة وهي اللغة العربية الفصحى الحديثة المعروفة أيضًا باسم MSA لكن عندما يتعلق الأمر بنطق MSA ، فإن مواهب التعليق الصوتي اللبناني هي الأفضل في الMSA ، لأنه على عكس اللهجات العربية الأخرى، فإن اللهجة اللبنانية لديها كل الحروف المشتركة مع ال MSA . هذا هو السبب في أنّ Belfay Studios، مع طاقم الممثلين اللبنانيين المحترفين ، وخبرة 25 عامًا في الدبلجة العربية يمكن أن تنجز أعمال الدبلجة العربية بأفضل طريقة ممكنة.

مع كل الاحترام لستديوهات التسجيل العربية.

اللغة العربية الفصحى الحديثة لسوقٍ أوسع وأكثر انتشارًا في مجال الدبلجة العربية.

title: How Arabic dubbing is still running amidst the Coronavirus lockdown
header: How Arabic dubbing is still running amidst the Coronavirus lockdown
summary: To all our dearest clients and partners, we at Belfay Studios would like to inform you that with all the restrictions that were caused by the Coronavirus lockdown on business operations worldwide, our team is doing a great job at keeping…
content:
How Arabic dubbing is still running amidst the Coronavirus lockdown.

To all our dearest clients and partners, we at Belfay Studios would like to inform you that with all the restrictions that were caused by the Coronavirus lockdown on business operations worldwide, our team is doing a great job at keeping the workflow just like it used to be while carefully following social distancing rules. As all of you know that in dubbing industry there is a part of the work that doesn’t require recording studios and voice-over talents, but could be done at home, such as translation, subtitling, Arabic diacritics, proofreading, quality control, as recorded script and more. For instance, our translation team is taking care of all the translation work that we have while staying at home in the same way our subtitling and proofreading team are getting the job done without facing any problems. However, we have some projects still underway at the studio since before the spread of the Coronavirus in Lebanon, thus we are making sure that these projects will be delivered as scheduled by using the right methods to keep our team and our dubbing talents safe. Separate work shifts are being appointed to each individual voice-over actor with the purpose of avoiding any risk of Coronavirus infection among our team and valuable actors while keeping our recording studios active so that we could keep providing the Arab World with all the entertainment they need in these tough times through all the documentaries, TV shows, series, video games, audio books, and cartoon shows that we’re working on. We would like to add that we are completely aware of the difficulties that everyone is facing around the globe and we hope for safety and good health for our partners and clients in the US, Spain, Italy, Germany, UK and everywhere else in the world.

Stay home, stay safe.

title: AI Dubbing vs Human Actors: Can Artificial Intelligence Replace Voice Actors?
header: AI Dubbing vs Human Actors: Can Artificial Intelligence Replace Voice Actors?
summary: Can AI truly replace human actors in dubbing? Discover why emotion, acting and human interaction remain essential to authentic Arabic dubbing.
content:
ألدبلجة بواسطة ال AI مقابل الدبلجة بأصوات ممثلين محترفين.

مع كل تطور جديد في الذكاء الاصطناعي، يطرح السؤال نفسه: هل أصبح بإمكان ال AI أن يحل مكان الممثل في الدبلجة؟ صحيح أن الـAI قادر اليوم على تسريع الترجمة وبعض المراحل التقنية، لكن هل الدبلجة مجرد كلمات وصوت؟ أم أنها إحساس وأداء وتمثيل؟ فالمشاهد لا يتعلق بشخصية بسبب الصوت فقط بل بسبب صدق المشاعر والأحاسيس، الشيء الذي لا يمكن استبداله بصوت آليّ. وهنا يأتي دور الممثل والمخرج؛ أحدهما يعيش الشخصية، والآخر يقوده لاكتشاف أدق تفاصيلها . قد تستطيع الآلة تقليد نبرة الغضب أو الحزن، لكن هل تفهم فعلًا ما الذي يجعلنا نصدق هذا الغضب أو نتأثر بذلك الحزن؟ وربما السؤال الأهم: لو أُعيدت دبلجة أعمالنا المفضلة بالكامل بالذكاء الاصطناعي، هل كانت ستبقى عالقة في ذاكرتنا كما هي اليوم؟ التكنولوجيا تتطور بسرعة، لكن الفرق كبير بين إنتاج صوت... وصناعة أداء.
بلفاي ستديوز.

With every new development in artificial intelligence, the same question arises: Has AI now become capable of replacing the actor in dubbing?

It is true that AI is now capable of speeding up translation and some of the technical stages, but is dubbing simply about words and voice? Or is it about emotion, performance, and acting?

A viewer does not become attached to a character because of the voice alone, but because of the authenticity of the emotions and feelings—something that cannot be replaced by an artificial voice.

And this is where the role of the actor and the director comes in: one lives the character, while the other guides them in discovering its finest details.

A machine may be able to imitate the tone of anger or sadness, but does it truly understand what makes us believe that anger or feel moved by that sadness?

Perhaps the most important question is this: If our favorite productions were completely redubbed using artificial intelligence, would they remain as deeply embedded in our memories as they are today?

Technology is evolving rapidly, but there is a significant difference between producing a voice... and creating a performance.

BELFAY STUDIOS
